## Seat review — ⭐ **ACCEPT.** It measured the card's own confidence gap, and the answer is worse than the card guessed.

`domain:ui` PM seat, `session_01UzHd6hDYatoDn17BuwKxnZ`. Reviewed at source on the branch, ⛔ not on the report. Merge-base `c736084bf`.

```ts
- const merged = { ...(schema.filter || {}), ...baseFilter };
+ const merged = composeDrillFilter(schema.filter, baseFilter);
```

## ⭐ The reach was the card's stated gap, and it is now measured

The card said in as many words: *"I did **not** measure the reach: whether any live pivot in the corpus authors the array form."* That gap is closed, and it does not resolve the comfortable way:

- ⭐ **`ElementDataSourceGate` writes the array arm mechanically.** Verified independently at source: `packages/react/src/element-data-source/ElementDataSourceGate.tsx` imports `mergeFilterNodes`, and its own docblock states component filter, view filter and binding filter *"all AND together through"* it. ⇒ a pivot bound the spec way (`dataSource {object, view}`) gets `schema.filter` set to an **AST node** — for **every saved view carrying a filter**.
- `object-pivot`'s **registry inputs advertise `filter` as type `array`**.
- Census of **43** in-repo pivot nodes: 5 sit near a filter key, and **every one is the array arm**.

⇒ **not one authors the object form** — the exact opposite of the chart's corpus, which is what made objectui#9016's "unreachable here" read plausible. The array arm is not an exotic authoring; it is the **mechanical default** for a spec-bound pivot.

⚠️ My own probe for that writer looked in `packages/app-shell` and came back empty. That was **my path guess, not evidence** — the file is in `packages/react`, and a repo-wide control (51 files) is what let me find it. Same class as the five instrument failures this seat has logged today.

## ⭐ Both stop conditions cleared by measurement, not by argument

**1.** *"Stop if routing through the seam changes the drilled row set for the object form."* ⇒ under ablation the object-arm's **row-set assertion stays GREEN** and only its shape assertion reds. The seam does not move the rows for the object dialect. That is the right way to retire a stop condition.

**2.** *"Stop if declaring `filter` on `PivotTableSchema` would narrow what an author can write."* ⇒ no declaration was added at all (**0** `packages/types` / `.zod.` files in the diff), and the reason is one I had not anticipated: **`PivotTableSchema` is `type: 'pivot'`** — the plain cross-tab, which reads **no filter at all**. Declaring it there would put an object-pivot-only key on the one node type that never reads it, **and still leave `object-pivot` undeclared**, since an object-pivot node is not assignable to that type literal. ⛔ Wrong twice over.

⚠️ My `Clause-②: yes` therefore turns out to have been **conservative**. That is the correct direction to be wrong in — a `no` that became false is the failure the rule guards; a `yes` that needed no carrier costs only a cheap review.

## ⭐ Two ablation readings that correct the card

**The pre-fix value fails differently at each sink**, which the card flattened into one word:

| sink | pre-fix behaviour with an array `schema.filter` |
|---|---|
| `ValueDataSource` | **refuses** an array comparand outside `$in`/`$nin`/`$between` ⇒ **excludes every row** (ablated array cases read `[]`) |
| `serializeDrillFilterParams` | **skips** a bare array comparand ⇒ no `filter[0]` written ⇒ the list lands scoped by the clicked cell alone — **this** is the superset the card names |

⇒ "returns a superset" is true at **one** of two sinks; at the other it returns **nothing**. Both are recorded in the pin's docblock, and the assertions stay on the conjunction so a red names the drop whichever sink resolved it.

**A real behaviour change, measured and pinned rather than assumed byte-identical:** a pivot cell click derives **two** conditions (row field and column field) which are themselves a conjunction, so a pivot with no filter of its own now drills by `{$and:[{stage:'won'},{source:'web'}]}` where the spread produced one flat object. ⚠️ ⛔ **Not** byte-identical — unlike `ObjectChart`, whose click context is a single key. The pin asserts both select the **same rows through the same matcher**, which is the right oracle for a shape change that must not be a behaviour change.

## The third site, and the one I asked you to check properly

⭐ **`ObjectMetricWidget` is NOT a third copy** — and this is the answer to the check I explicitly refused to pre-empt. It composes nothing: it hands its own `resolvedFilter` to `DrillDownDrawer` as a **single source**, with a comment stating `drillDown.filter` is deliberately not forwarded, and it calls neither `computeDrillFilter` nor `composeDrillFilter`. ⭐ Correct for a KPI whose whole tile **is** the slice. My one-spelling probe was right by luck; this is right by reading.

⭐ **objectui#9137 filed — the third site, and the worst of the three.** `buildDatasetDrillFilter` ends with `return runtimeFilter ? { ...runtimeFilter, ...drillFilter } : drillFilter`, and `DashboardWidgetSchema.filter`'s **own docblock** says objectui passes an ObjectQL FilterNode **array** there. Deduped against objectui#9085 — a *different* defect in the same function whose repair would not repair this.

The oracle is the composed filter's **row set**, with a fixture where the pivot filter sits on a field that is **neither axis**, so losing it demonstrably moves the rows. Ablation: 8 of 9 red, the one green being the live control **by design** — which is what proves the reds are about the composition and not the harness.

## Contract review

**Reviewed head:** `40453be9f` (fix committed first, so the ablation's restore leg pointed at a real commit) · **Card:** objectui#9024

### ① Derived judgments
⛔ **No declaration moves.** 0 files under `packages/types` or `*.zod.*`; `filter?: any` stays a local props member for the reason above. The change routes an existing composition through `composeDrillFilter`, which takes `unknown`. Both dialects the component already read continue to be accepted; the object arm's rows are unchanged, the array arm's stop being dropped. ⇒ a **repair**, not an accept-set move.

### ② Semver

| ⚠️ NOT MEASURED, declared | `check:sdui-registration-pins` exits **2** — "no console build to weigh". This diff adds no registration; left to CI, ⛔ not read as a pass |

## ⛔ The open question is NOT mine to rule — routing it

`object-pivot` has no `Object*Schema` of its own: `objectName`, `dataProvider` and `filter` all live on a local props intersection (the objectui#6357 second-declaration class). ⭐ Nine of eleven sibling `Object*Schema` interfaces declare `filter` on their own interface; this one has none.

⇒ adding `ObjectPivotTableSchema` to `@object-ui/types` is a **published authorable surface widening** — a public-contract change, which sits on this lane's **manual floor**. ⛔ Not a dev's judgement and ⛔ not this seat's.

**Seat recommendation: A**, with the dev's reasoning, which I have checked and agree with: it is what the other nine object-* widgets already do, it is the only option that puts the key on the node that **actually reads it**, and it settles `objectName` and `dataProvider` in the same stroke instead of leaving the same class open for two more rounds. ⭐ It is a **widening**, so it refuses nothing an author writes today. Going to the maintainer, ⛔ not blocking this PR.
